title: LQR control
equipment: Reduced body-bounce mode of an active road-vehicle suspension
physicalPurpose: Balance suspension travel, body motion, and hydraulic effort, then preserve the selected design when only noisy displacement is measured.
objective: Derive state feedback from declared state and effort costs.

simplifications: The two-state local body-bounce model omits the tyre, unsprung mass, hydraulic actuator dynamics, pitch, roll, delay and structural modes.
Equivalent simulator copies separate clean validation state from the noisy position-only sensor record.
The road event is a bounded equivalent vertical-acceleration pulse rather than measured tyre-profile geometry.
The steady-state Kalman gain assumes the declared linear model and covariance and is not an online covariance estimator.
Simulation evidence does not qualify a physical suspension, actuator, sensor, road profile or vehicle.

baseline.limitation: Pole placement stabilizes the local mode but does not encode a reproducible preference among suspension travel, body motion and hydraulic effort.

change.decision: Select a regulator only from common physical tradeoff measures, then accept position-only LQG only when estimator and abnormal-case evidence remain inside declared bounds.

disturbances: Apply +0.5 m/s2 road-equivalent acceleration from 1.0 through 1.5 seconds.
Compare pole placement and all four full-state LQR candidates from identical state, seed, event, limits and interval.
Compare balanced full-state LQR with balanced position-only LQG.
Repeat LQG with 0.004 m position noise and with the declared spring/damping mismatch.

abortPredicates: Any required signal is nonfinite, stale, forced, invalid, missing or bound to the wrong simulator copy.
Applied force, road acceleration, suspension deflection or body velocity leaves its declared local range.
A comparison changes model, interval, initial state, event, seed, limit or an undeclared weight.
The position-only LQG calculation reads validation velocity truth.
Force saturation occurs where unconstrained LQR optimality is claimed.
safety.restorationMode: Remove the road request, disable hydraulic control, verify exactly zero applied force, then reset both simulator copies and estimator state.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised vehicle-controls engineer with the responsible hydraulic, mechanical, test-track and functional-safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Clean state, exact model matrices and deterministic noise are Simulation validation data.
No vehicle, suspension actuator, hydraulic system or road-test equipment is operated.
Physical use requires identified full-order dynamics, calibrated sensing, actuator and structural limits, reviewed containment, explicit immediate approval and rollback.

video.viewerOutcome: Turn explicit suspension-motion and force preferences into qualified LQR gains, then decide whether position-only LQG preserves the selected design.

learning.context: A reduced active-suspension body mode must reject one common road pulse with bounded hydraulic force.
learning.reason: Pole placement does not express the desired state-versus-effort trade, and a physical controller may not measure every required state.
theory: State and input weights give a quadratic cost a declared engineering meaning only after unit scaling is handled.
The Riccati solution produces the optimal unconstrained state-feedback gain for one declared linear model and cost.
Common physical measures, rather than each candidate's private cost, support the engineering selection.
LQG combines the selected LQR with a covariance-qualified state estimate but inherits model, noise and constraint limitations.
learning.workedPrediction: At z=0.03 m and v=0, pole placement requests -0.39000 kN while body-motion, travel, balanced and effort-saving LQR request -0.03495, -0.16694, -0.06594 and -0.01456 kN.
practicalPreparation: Verify model, interval, state, road event, seed, selector, force limits, estimator initialization and Simulation-only truth labels.
Inspect normalized preferences and their dimensional Q/R transformation before comparing solved gains.
learning.baseline: Execute pole-placement gain [13,6] as a stable but preference-implicit causal baseline.
learning.change: Execute four independently solved LQR gains, select from common physical measures, then combine the balanced gain with the position-only Kalman estimator.
learning.comparison: Compare deflection, velocity, acceleration, force energy, force movement, peak force, saturation and return time under one common road pulse, then add estimation error and innovation for LQG.
learning.validation: Accept only finite, unsaturated, locally valid records whose regulator, estimator, nominal and abnormal evidence satisfy the declared requirements.
learning.explanation: Weights express preferences, Riccati equations solve the declared unconstrained problem, and estimator error enters force when complete state is unavailable.
